title: Felix and the Border
premise: Elodie Amberdale, a financial-crimes investigator who once trained inside a covert laundering network called the Border, has spent seven years on the right side of the ledger — until a real-estate listing for her old safe house surfaces with interior photos that include a woman who shouldn't exist: herself. Pulled back into the world she escaped, she discovers the Border is being dismantled from within by its own architect, and that her former mentor, Marek Voss, is using her old case files to hunt the trainees one by one. With the help of her handler Tomas Reyes and a rogue analyst, Junie, Elodie must trace the network's money backward through seven years of clean transactions to expose the training program before Voss erases every witness, including her. In the end she chooses love and found family over the duty that made her, burning the Border's ledger publicly at the cost of her career, and walking away with the people who chose to stand beside her.
about_author: Ansel Iversen is the pen name of a former compliance officer who spent a decade tracing money across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers from a small house near the northern coast, where the fog does most of the editing.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Scrolling listings after a long day of clearing legitimate funds, Elodie freezes: a familiar safe house, photographed from inside, and in one image a reflection of a woman wearing her old jacket. The listing vanishes within the hour. Emotional beat: the past tapping on glass.

chapters.title: Clean Hands
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. At the Financial Integrity Unit, Elodie's caseload is all boring, legitimate money — deliberately so, she suspects. She pulls the safe house's ownership chain and finds a shell company she recognizes from training. Her request to investigate is denied within minutes. Emotional beat: the walls of her orderly life showing hairline cracks.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Handler Tomas Reyes notices Elodie's unauthorized queries and covers for her — then finds his own access logs altered. Someone inside the agency is watching them both. He warns her off, but hands her an old burner number anyway. Emotional beat: loyalty tested before it's asked for.

chapters.title: What the Border Taught Me
chapters.summary: POV Elodie, interwoven flashbacks. Seven years ago, Elodie trained at the Border: a school for laundering, run with tenderness and terror by Marek Voss, who called his students 'children of the ledger.' She defected when a classmate, Ines, was disappeared. Emotional beat: memory as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: The Second Photograph
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. A second listing appears — a different safe house, and in the photos, a body laid out on the kitchen floor, face turned away. Elodie recognizes the room, then the shoes. Ines is dead, or was, years ago. Emotional beat: grief arriving late and doubled.

chapters.title: Junie
chapters.summary: POV Junie. Rogue analyst Junie Okafor, who monitors real-estate data for fun, traced the listings to a pattern: every property once used by the Border, listed in reverse order of Elodie's training timeline. Someone is walking the network backward toward her. Emotional beat: two strangers realizing they're in the same trap.

chapters.title: Rules That Keep Getting Rewritten
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. New compliance directives arrive that would legally forbid the agency from investigating the Border — drafted, Tomas discovers, by a consultancy that once laundered through it. The rules were written by the crime. Emotional beat: the vertigo of institutional betrayal.

chapters.title: The Safe House Burns
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Elodie and Junie reach the listed safe house first and find it mid-fire, arson timed to their arrival. In the ashes, a single unburnt page: a training ledger page with Elodie's student number circled. Voss isn't hiding her past — he's advertising it. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Children of the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Elodie, flashback-heavy. The training years in full: Voss's doctrine that money is memory and memory can be laundered; the night Elodie chose to run and Ines chose to stay. Elodie admits to Junie why she never looked back. Emotional beat: confession as armor removal.

chapters.title: Backward Through the Money
chapters.summary: POV Junie. Junie maps seven years of the Border's cleaned transactions, finding they all terminate in one account: the agency's own seized-assets fund. The network was never dismantled; it was absorbed. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of everything Elodie served.

chapters.title: The Handler's Dilemma
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Tomas is ordered to bring Elodie in for 'protective custody' — a euphemism he recognizes. He stalls, burns a favor, and instead meets her in person for the first time in years, choosing her over the institution. Emotional beat: duty inverted into devotion.

chapters.title: Voss, Alive
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. A dead-drop message in Voss's unmistakable hand offers a meeting: he claims he built the listings to flush out the Border's new owners, and he needs the student who escaped to read the ledger. Elodie doesn't trust him — but the handwriting is real. Emotional beat: the old gravity of a mentor's pull.

chapters.title: The Meeting at the Border
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. At the abandoned original training house, Voss reveals the network survived him and now runs through the agency's seized-assets fund — and that the purge of former trainees is to bury the program's existence. He is dying and wants his ledger burned publicly. Emotional beat: hate and grief sharing a table.

chapters.title: Ines's File
chapters.summary: POV Junie. Junie decrypts Ines's file from the ledger: Ines didn't betray Elodie — she stayed as a double agent and was killed by the network's new director, who signs as 'Caretaker.' The Caretaker's identity is redacted, but the clearance level is Tomas's. Emotional beat: suspicion poisoning the found family.

chapters.title: Confrontation on the Stairwell
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Elodie accuses Tomas; he proves his logs were forged but realizes who could forge them — his deputy, Rell, the Caretaker's inside man. Before they can act, Rell locks down the building. Emotional beat: trust nearly destroyed, then reforged under pressure.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: POV Elodie and Tomas, alternating. Trapped in the agency building during a staged security incident, they move through service corridors while Rell hunts them with the building's own systems. Junie, outside, works the digital locks from a café laptop. Emotional beat: the found family functioning as one organism.

chapters.title: What the Caretaker Wants
chapters.summary: POV Rell. The Caretaker's design revealed: not money, but precedent — a world where compliance itself launders, and no investigator can ever again follow money home. Elodie is the last living witness who can testify the program existed. Emotional beat: evil as architecture, not appetite.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Voss delivers the physical ledger — every trainee, every account, seven years of the Border — and tells her the only safe place for it is in the open. He stays behind as bait. Emotional beat: inheritance of a terrible gift, accepted.

chapters.title: Burning the Border
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Climax. Elodie broadcasts the ledger to every regulator, journalist, and trainee on the list simultaneously, forcing the Caretaker's hand; Rell moves to kill her at the old safe house, and Tomas and Junie intervene. Voss dies holding the door. The Caretaker's identity — a founding 'reformer' of the agency — goes public with the ledger. Emotional beat: love against duty, resolved by choosing both people and truth.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV Junie. Hearings begin; the seized-assets fund is frozen; Rell cooperates for leniency. Elodie is dismissed for cause — the institution protecting itself one last time — and finds she feels lighter than she has in seven years. Emotional beat: exile as release.

chapters.title: The House That Was Listed
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Elodie, Tomas, and Junie buy the original safe house with pooled money — the first property in the chain with a clean, honest deed. They repaint, repair the fire damage to the last one, and plant something where the ledger burned. Emotional beat: found family, given an address.

chapters.title: Felix
chapters.summary: POV Elodie, coda. The stray cat that haunted the safe house in her training years — Felix, the one creature Voss was soft with — returns and stays. Elodie writes her resignation letter as a confession and mails it to no one, then closes the door on the Border forever. Final beat: memory kept, duty laid down, love remaining.
